title: Surgery through history
examples: What was the biggest change in surgery before Lister?
How did anaesthesia change surgery for people?
What is the difference between antiseptic and sterile?

explain.say: Today we will say about surgery through history. We will learn about big changes in medicine.
First we learn about anaesthesia. This means making people feel no pain during surgery. Before this, surgery was very painful for everyone.
Next we look at antiseptics. These are substances that kill germs on skin and tools. This helped stop many dangerous infections from spreading.
Next we learn about Lister. He was very important because he used antiseptics in surgery. This greatly improved patient survival rates.
Our next step is keyhole surgery. This means making very small cuts to reach the problem area. It is much less invasive than big cuts.
In everyday life, think about getting a small cyst removed. Before keyhole surgery, they might make a large cut. Now, they use a small keyhole cut for better healing.

draw.text: Real life: Small cuts heal better

faq.q: Why was anaesthesia so important for surgery?
faq.a: Anaesthesia was important because it stopped the patient from feeling pain during the operation. Before it, surgery was extremely traumatic for the person undergoing it.
asks: Why is pain relief needed in surgery?

faq.q: What is the difference between antiseptic and sterile?
faq.a: Antiseptics are substances used to clean and kill germs on living tissue. Sterility means an object is completely free from all living germs.
asks: Are antiseptics the same as sterilizing?
How do I keep things germ-free?

faq.q: Who was Lister and what did he introduce?
faq.a: Lister introduced the use of antiseptics into surgical practice. He helped prove that germs caused infections after surgery.
asks: What did Lister discover about germs?
Why is Lister's name important in medicine?

faq.a: Keyhole surgery uses very small cuts, or incisions, to perform the operation. This results in less damage to the body and quicker recovery.

faq.q: Did medicine change quickly after anaesthesia?
faq.a: Yes, the introduction of anaesthesia led to a huge focus on preventing infection. This brought the use of antiseptics and better surgical techniques.
asks: What followed the discovery of pain relief?
Was the change in surgery sudden?

facts: Anaesthesia allowed surgeons to operate without causing pain.
Antiseptics were used to clean wounds and surgical tools.
Joseph Lister was key in applying antiseptic principles to surgery.
Keyhole surgery uses small incisions for minimally invasive procedures.

quiz.say: What major breakthrough allowed surgeons to operate without causing pain?
quiz.why: Anaesthesia directly addresses the problem of surgical pain.

wrong.1: Antiseptics stop infection, but they do not stop pain.
wrong.2: Keyhole surgery is about small cuts, not pain relief.
wrong.3: Lister focused on germ control, not pain management.

quiz.say: Which method focuses on killing germs on wounds and tools?
quiz.why: Antiseptics are defined as substances used to kill germs on surfaces.

wrong.0: Keyhole surgery is a technique, not a germ killer.
wrong.1: Sterilizing is a process, but antiseptics are the substances used.
wrong.3: Anaesthesia affects the patient's feeling, not the germs.

quiz.say: A surgeon uses very small cuts to remove a kidney. This technique is called:
quiz.why: Keyhole surgery specifically describes using small incisions for less damage.

wrong.0: An antiseptic wash is a cleaning agent, not a surgical method.
wrong.1: Anaesthesia is about keeping the patient unconscious.
wrong.3: Open surgery involves making large, noticeable cuts.
